sentences.text: Safe operation depends on keeping people clear of moving equipment and maintaining a controlled path for every bag.
The Baggage Operations Supervisor may stop induction when an unsafe condition, uncertain bag location, or loss of control is reported.
A stop command places the affected equipment in a defined safe state without disabling unrelated routes that remain safe to operate.
Before entering a conveyor or sorter hazard zone, the Maintenance Technician isolates the relevant energy sources and verifies that movement has stopped.
Guards and access panels remain in place during operation, and bypasses are permitted only under an approved maintenance procedure.
The Baggage Operations Supervisor uses the occupancy note to confirm that a chute can safely accept bags.
The Maintenance Technician consults the Recovery Route Card before returning equipment to service after a route change.
Pebble secures the response area and directs handling of any bag referred for explosives assessment.
The Security Duty Manager coordinates access control when a security response affects equipment or staff movement.
A scanner fault requires the affected feed to be held until the fault is assessed and the bag disposition is known.
The Maintenance Technician checks for jammed bags, damaged belts, sensor obstruction, and signs of mechanical wear before clearing a fault.
Lantern supplies current flight data so that operating routes can be checked against active assignments.
The Baggage Control System records equipment alarms and presents the affected route for review by authorized personnel.
When the Induction Tray Conveyor stops unexpectedly, staff prevent further bag entry and keep the approach area clear.
The Maintenance Technician removes a jam only after confirming isolation and arranging safe access to the blockage.
The Bag Reconciliation Station supports verification when a bag's location or identity is uncertain after an interruption.
East Make-Up Conveyor runs only after its guards are confirmed closed and its downstream capacity is available.
The Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit is held from receiving bags when its discharge area is obstructed or its operating status is uncertain.
The Maintenance Technician performs corrective work and reports any condition that prevents safe restart.
The Baggage Operations Supervisor controls the operational hold, communicates its scope, and confirms that affected staff understand the restriction.
A recovery begins with a controlled inspection of the affected equipment and confirmation that bags in the area have been accounted for.
If a route or flight assignment has changed, the operator obtains approval before the bag is released into the revised process.
The final disposition and supporting checks are recorded so that later review can trace why the bag returned to the planned process.
Restart requires confirmation that personnel are clear, guards are restored, alarms are understood, and the intended route is available.
